\frac{(x+p)(x+q)(x+15)}{(x+4)^2} = 0
\]
has exactly \(3\) distinct roots, while the equation 
\[
\frac{(x+2p)(x+4)(x+9)}{(x+q)(x+15)} = 0
\]
has exactly \(2\) distinct roots. Compute \(100p + q.\)
Facts: Set_Cardinality(Solve_equation(x: Real, (x + 2*p) * (x + 4) * (x + 9) / ((x + q) * (x + 15)) = 0)) = 2; Set_Cardinality(Solve_equation(x: Real, (x + p) * (x + q) * (x + 15) / ((x + 4)^2) = 0)) = 3
